    "title": "Mover model: startup Cube ruined renders, sunk eye spheres, Mirror broke the ragdoll",
    "content": "Two bugs in Mover.fbx that were invisible in the outliner and obvious once rendered, plus the structural fix that unblocked the ragdoll.\n\n1. THE STARTUP CUBE. Blender's default startup file ships a 2m Cube at the origin. It swallowed the character from the knees down in every turnaround render, and the previews still looked deliberate - the model appeared to be standing in a white box, so the earlier session never noticed and reported the model as done. render_preview.py now has hide_non_mover(), which sets hide_render on everything that is not in the MOVER collection (skipping cameras and lights). Always hide non-asset objects before rendering rather than trusting a clean scene.\n\n2. FACE DECALS ERUPTING THROUGH THE SKULL. The eyes were UV spheres sunk into the head ellipsoid. Verified numerically: EyeWhite's worst corner evaluated to 1.368 and Pupil's to 1.159 against the ellipsoid equation (must be <= 1.0), so both burst out the sides of the head as a pale band - which reads as a bandage or mask. Root cause: to be visible from the front a sunk sphere must clear the surface, and by then its outer edge is outside the skull. Fix is a face_decal() helper that computes the ellipsoid surface point for a given x,z offset, orients a THIN CYLINDER to the local surface normal there, and sits it just proud. Cannot poke out sideways by construction. selfcheck() now asserts every EyeWhite/Pupil vertex is within 1.28 of the ellipsoid equation and is called from __main__.\n\n3. MIRROR MODIFIER BROKE THE RAGDOLL - the important one. The generator built only the +X half and used a Mirror modifier. export_fbx uses use_mesh_modifiers=True, which BAKES the mirror into ONE mesh, so the FBX contained a single 'Thigh', a single 'Hand' and so on: 29 objects with no L/R pair anywhere. In Unity that becomes ONE rigidbody for both legs and the character cannot move its legs independently. Rewrote as build_side(sx, sfx) called for ('L') and ('R') to make every limb its own object: now 62 objects with ThighL/ThighR, ShinL/ShinR, BootL/BootR, UpperArmL/R, ForearmL/R, HandL/R. Mirror is still fine for static props; never for anything that will be simulated.\n\nAlso: never name a cosmetic part after a simulated part. BuildRagdoll.cs matches by name prefix, so the old 'BootToe' decoration would have received its own rigidbody. Renamed to ToeCap/Sole/Knee, and a RIDES_ON table parents each cosmetic to the limb it rides on (longest-prefix match so 'PackStrap' is not claimed by 'Pack').\n\nDetail work that answered the 'ugly / no details' complaint: added Nose, Mouth, Brow (brows create the expression - eyes alone still read as a mannequin), Collar, Pocket, PocketFlap, Pouch, PouchFlap, Sole, Knee, Patch. Saturated the palette because a mid-grey preview washes pastels out. Shortened arms from 0.30/0.28 to 0.24/0.21 - realistic limb length on a 3.5-head chibi figure reads as an ape, hands should end at the hip. Collar radius had to drop from TORSO_W*0.30 to *0.26 because the head is an ellipsoid and its half-width at collar height is ~0.149, not HEAD_W/2 = 0.23.\n\nFinal: 62 objects, ~6456 tris, selfcheck passes. Commit d165af1. BuildRagdoll.cs and Ragdoll.cs were both updated for the new per-side names (Ragdoll used a Contains(\"Hand\")+\"L\"/\"R\" heuristic that would have matched the wrong object).",

    "title": "Mover model: startup Cube ruined renders, sunk eye spheres, Mirror broke the ragdoll",
    "content": "Two bugs in Mover.fbx that were invisible in the outliner and obvious once rendered, plus the structural fix that unblocked the ragdoll.\n\n1. THE STARTUP CUBE. Blender's default startup file ships a 2m Cube at the origin. It swallowed the character from the knees down in every turnaround render, and the previews still looked deliberate - the model appeared to be standing in a white box, so the earlier session never noticed and reported the model as done. render_preview.py now has hide_non_mover(), which sets hide_render on everything that is not in the MOVER collection (skipping cameras and lights). Always hide non-asset objects before rendering rather than trusting a clean scene.\n\n2. FACE DECALS ERUPTING THROUGH THE SKULL. The eyes were UV spheres sunk into the head ellipsoid. Verified numerically: EyeWhite's worst corner evaluated to 1.368 and Pupil's to 1.159 against the ellipsoid equation (must be <= 1.0), so both burst out the sides of the head as a pale band - which reads as a bandage or mask. Root cause: to be visible from the front a sunk sphere must clear the surface, and by then its outer edge is outside the skull. Fix is a face_decal() helper that computes the ellipsoid surface point for a given x,z offset, orients a THIN CYLINDER to the local surface normal there, and sits it just proud. Cannot poke out sideways by construction. selfcheck() now asserts every EyeWhite/Pupil vertex is within 1.28 of the ellipsoid equation and is called from __main__.\n\n3. MIRROR MODIFIER BROKE THE RAGDOLL - the important one. The generator built only the +X half and used a Mirror modifier. export_fbx uses use_mesh_modifiers=True, which BAKES the mirror into ONE mesh, so the FBX contained a single 'Thigh', a single 'Hand' and so on: 29 objects with no L/R pair anywhere. In Unity that becomes ONE rigidbody for both legs and the character cannot move its legs independently. Rewrote as build_side(sx, sfx) called for ('L') and ('R') to make every limb its own object: now 62 objects with ThighL/ThighR, ShinL/ShinR, BootL/BootR, UpperArmL/R, ForearmL/R, HandL/R. Mirror is still fine for static props; never for anything that will be simulated.\n\nAlso: never name a cosmetic part after a simulated part. BuildRagdoll.cs matches by name prefix, so the old 'BootToe' decoration would have received its own rigidbody. Renamed to ToeCap/Sole/Knee, and a RIDES_ON table parents each cosmetic to the limb it rides on (longest-prefix match so 'PackStrap' is not claimed by 'Pack').\n\nDetail work that answered the 'ugly / no details' complaint: added Nose, Mouth, Brow (brows create the expression - eyes alone still read as a mannequin), Collar, Pocket, PocketFlap, Pouch, PouchFlap, Sole, Knee, Patch. Saturated the palette because a mid-grey preview washes pastels out. Shortened arms from 0.30/0.28 to 0.24/0.21 - realistic limb length on a 3.5-head chibi figure reads as an ape, hands should end at the hip. Collar radius had to drop from TORSO_W*0.30 to *0.26 because the head is an ellipsoid and its half-width at collar height is ~0.149, not HEAD_W/2 = 0.23.\n\nFinal: 62 objects, ~6456 tris, selfcheck passes. Commit d165af1. BuildRagdoll.cs and Ragdoll.cs were both updated for the new per-side names (Ragdoll used a Contains(\"Hand\")+\"L\"/\"R\" heuristic that would have matched the wrong object).",
